doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: One week with Sammy Davis Jr.
summary: Pallo's story of the pile of charts and changing arrangements on a week with Sammy Davis Jr.'s orchestra.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Oh sure. The best I think I have to say, talking about different people, Sammy Davis Jr. was one of the most fabulous entertainers in the world I think, as far as entertaining. He did everything. And playing with Sammy Davis, oh I have a good story for you. I only did one week with Sammy Davis and the music would be piled up this high, and we would rehearse the — George Rhodes I think was the orchestra that I played with. And we would have all the charts set for the show. Sammy would come out and start the show and they would change “What Kind of Fool Am I” to a different rendition. Now he had about five different arrangements of “What Kind of Fool am I.” One was for T.V., one was for live, one is a short rendition or whatever. And I had the one we rehearsed. And now I’m going through this pile of music we did already and halfway through the song I’m looking for the song because they changed the chart, and to go through this music, you’re fiddling through and Johnny Mendoza was the rhythm/percussion, and he says, “Lou, don’t worry about it just play the other chart and then fake it.” And that’s what I had to do. Because the music was piled so high. And then playing for Sammy Davis the thing, I love a good entertainer and watching Sammy perform, it’s hard to watch him and watch what your cues are going to be next. And I tried to watch, he was just fabulous, fabulous. And he played drums too. He came back, played drums. But he was great. A great entertainer.
That is really hard to do, to keep your eye on the music when you’re playing with some legend out there.
And you’re trying to see, because I’d rather be out in the audience watching him. I really would. But you can’t, you have to pay attention to the chart.
